reason: Start assembling the digestive tract by connecting the salivary glands to the mouth.
expectation: The glands will fill their slot on the digestive tube, with their ducts opening into the mouth.

alternatives.reason: Starch digestion is also a goal, but I prefer to begin with the anatomy.

effect: The salivary glands are fitted; the other organs still need connecting.
reason: Continue assembling the digestive tract by connecting the pancreas.
expectation: The pancreas will fill its slot, with its duct leading to the small intestine.

effect: The pancreas is fitted; the liver and gallbladder remain to be connected.
reason: Continue assembling the digestive system by fitting the liver and gallbladder.
expectation: They will fill their slot, with bile ducts leading toward the intestine.

effect: The gland and organ fitting goal is complete; digestion remains.
reaction: The summary usefully connects the organs to their secretions.
reason: Start breaking down the starchy food with salivary amylase.
expectation: Amylase will begin breaking starch into smaller carbohydrates, probably requiring further digestion.

effect: Salivary amylase shortened the starch chains; further digestion is now available.
reaction: The intermediate makes the staged breakdown clear.
reason: Continue breaking down the starch toward absorbable sugars.
expectation: The enzymes will break the shorter chains into smaller sugars, possibly glucose.

effect: The starch is now individual glucose molecules, ready for absorption; protein and fat digestion remain.
reaction: The two-stage starch breakdown was clear.
reason: Break down the protein food toward absorbable components.
expectation: The enzymes will cut the protein chains into smaller peptides or amino acids.

effect: Protein digestion produced amino acids; fat digestion remains.
reason: Use the only offered combination to break down the fat.
expectation: Bile will disperse the fat into smaller droplets, and lipase will break it into absorbable components.
